coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For When Fear
Gets Loud
coverDek: Five prayers for the kind of fear that doesn't ask permission — before a diagnosis, before a decision, before the phone rings. Five different voices, one steady God.

points.hook: Lord, I don't know what's coming, and tonight that's the whole problem.
paragraphs: I've run tomorrow through my mind a hundred different ways and none of them feel safe enough to rest in. But fear has never once changed what's coming — it's only ever changed how I slept the night before it arrived. So I'm laying the unknown down at Your feet exactly as uncertain as it is, choosing to trust the One who already knows how every version of tomorrow ends.
points.verseText: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee.

points.hook: I decree it today: their opinion of me does not get to run my life.
paragraphs: I break every snare set by the fear of man in the name of Jesus — the fear of being misunderstood, overlooked, or talked about! I was not created to manage every room's approval, and I refuse to shrink one more time just to stay likeable. My trust is in the Lord, and the Lord makes me safe — not safe from being disliked, but safe in who I actually am!
points.verseText: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe.

points.hook: Notice your chest right now. Notice your hands.
paragraphs: Fear doesn't just live in your thoughts — it lives in the tightness behind your ribs, the shallow breath, the heart that won't slow down even after the threat has passed. Jesus didn't just promise you a calmer mind; He left you His own peace, the kind that reaches a trembling body, not just a worried head. Breathe out as you pray this. Let your shoulders drop. That's not a coincidence — that's the peace arriving.
points.verseText: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you... let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.

points.hook: Somebody reading this is more afraid for someone else than for themselves.
paragraphs: You're not just carrying your own fear tonight — you're carrying it for a child still finding their way, a marriage under pressure, a parent whose health isn't what it used to be. Family, God's command to Joshua wasn't just for one man leading one nation — it's for every one of us standing watch over someone we love. Be strong. Be of good courage. The God who went with Joshua into unfamiliar land is going with the people you love into theirs.
points.verseText: Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.

points.hook: Close your eyes, child. I already know what's hiding in the dark, and it isn't bigger than Me.
paragraphs: You don't have to check the locks one more time tonight, or run through every worst case before you're allowed to rest. The terror that stalks the night and the arrow nobody sees coming by day are both already named, already measured, already smaller than the hand holding you. Sleep now. I'm not asking you to stop being afraid by willpower — I'm just asking you to let Me be bigger than whatever it is.
points.verseText: Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day.

cta.closingLine: If even one of these named the fear you've been carrying, don't just scroll past it — pray it out loud tonight. Come back tomorrow for the next series.
